title: Is this strategy generally profitable?
summary: I want to ask someone who's been options trading for a long time(at least for years).My concept is that when we trade regular stocks, if we hypothetically just wait for a huge stock drop(think of the doom drop when COVID happened or in the beginning of 2022) and then buy the extreme dip, we're kinda destined to make profit(I actually did buy a huge dip in early 2022 and made a lot of profits).Now I am thinking what if someone also waits for a huuge dip and then buys a really long term call option(like 3 months? 6months?) and just sells those options as soon as the price of the option contract goes up and makes a 20% profit. IF someone really adheres to this strategy very strictly, would that person most likely make profits?submitted by/u/cakewalk093[link][comments]
